_readme: SHARED FIXTURE for the both-forms-established predicate. Read by BOTH sides:
Oracle 2026-08-19: a fixture of plain uppercase rows CANNOT expose the divergence this pin
exists for. The engine's bucket keys are already _cmp_norm-collapsed; the JS value_counts
keys are raw. So the cases that matter are MIXED CASE and SEPARATOR/WHITESPACE VARIANTS —
'mixed_case_head' and 'separator_variant' below. Delete those two and the pin greens on a
real divergence. Every case states the answer AND why.

cases.name: clean single series — the round-9 Pelican corpus, nothing else confirmed
cases.head: P1
cases.why: no confirmed value starts P1; the misread form is not a convention

cases.name: the live mature install — three confirmed P1 mis-confirms at n=30
cases.head: P1
cases.why: bar = max(3, ceil(0.10*27)) = 3; same-head = 3 -> established, so the engine vetoes and the confirm path asks once

cases.name: just below the floor
cases.head: P1
cases.why: same-head = 2 < the absolute floor of 3 (the 10% leg would allow 2 at n=20 — the floor is what stops it)

cases.name: the 10% leg binds on a large scope — 21 sightings still is not a convention
cases.head: AB
cases.why: bar = max(3, ceil(0.10*221)) = 23; same-head = 21 < 23. Above the absolute floor of 3 the SHARE leg is what binds, so a big scope needs proportionally more evidence before a second form counts as established

cases.name: ...and the same scope one sighting over the line
cases.head: AB
cases.why: total 223, bar 23, same-head 23 -> established. The pair above/below pins WHERE the line sits, which a single case cannot

cases.name: mixed_case_head — THE PIN. Raw keys vs collapsed keys diverge here
cases.head: pi
cases.why: both keys normalise to the same head; a case-sensitive raw-key compare would count 3 and answer false

cases.name: separator_variant — THE OTHER PIN. Whitespace inside the value
cases.head: SB
cases.why: all three SB rows collapse to the same head so same-head = 4, but bar = max(3, ceil(0.10*44)) = 5 -> not established. A raw-key compare would ALSO answer false, for the wrong reason (it would see only 2) — the count is asserted separately in the suites

cases.name: empty head
cases.why: no head to test — never established

cases.name: empty corpus
cases.head: P1
cases.why: a fresh install has no history; both sides must answer false rather than divide by zero

cases.name: zero and negative counts are ignored, not summed
cases.head: P1
cases.why: a non-positive count is not evidence; it must not inflate the total either
